data.body: Operator 2026-11-11 (answering the coordinator's list of ddflow gaps after one day of about ten parallel agents). SUBJECT: what a coordinating agent retypes or polls by hand: ~1000 words of project rules in every agent brief, phase-close bookkeeping, a dashboard of lanes/suites/approvals, and polling for 'waiting on background work'. NAMED USER: the coordinator agent and the operator reading its reports. No open phase covers it: P-operator-digest is the operator's waiting-on-you queue, P-awareness is push to the operator, P-agent-parity is per-harness behaviour, P-wind-down is restart. FALSIFIER: wrong if, after CO-brief-roles and CO-lanes-coordinator land, coordinators still paste rules into briefs or poll lanes by hand. No phase needs on purpose: work here keeps no hold.
data.title: Coordination: a coordinator's view, built-in agent roles, phase close automation and event-driven wake-ups

data.alternatives: Run the full suite on every item (rejected: 40 minutes per item); trust the lane ci (rejected: partial ci passed both red merges); revert-on-red only (rejected: every lane still pays before the revert).
data.consequences: One more gate stage to maintain; a probe that is too slow or too narrow defeats it, so the budget is measured (GM-smoke-gate) and the module list is derived from the registries, not hand-kept.
data.context: Main went red twice in one day from merges with partial ci (tool-family import failing for ddflow_dispatch, then bandit B608); every lane then burned a 21600 s ci run that was dead on arrival.
data.decision: Before any full suite, merge (and ci) run a smoke gate of at most [smoke].budget_s (default 60 s): import probe of every module that registers tools, families, commands or events; ruff check and format --check on the changed files; bandit on the changed files; the item's own targeted tests. A smoke failure refuses the merge and never starts the 21600 s ci. The full suite runs once per main commit by the merge queue (BG-ci) and its result is stored per sha (GM-baseline-store). While main is red, merges are refused except from the item that fixes it; the red-main bug is filed automatically and its fix task gets the top priority band.
data.title: Merge is guarded by a seconds-long smoke gate; the full suite runs once per main commit in a queue; red main is a first-class priority

data.alternatives: Keep free-form forced with a longer reason (rejected: not checkable); refuse all forced completions (rejected: a red main must not block unrelated work).
data.consequences: Needs the per-sha baseline store (GM-baseline-store) and rerun-alone (GM-rerun-alone). The ids are only as good as the baseline run; B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause is a known limit and the evidence must record the failure text digest, not only the id.
data.context: Most phase closes in one day ran over a partial unit_tests under the standing approval window, so 'forced' no longer distinguishes a justified red baseline from a skipped check.
data.decision: A partial unit_tests that fails only on tests that also fail on the exact base sha is recorded as outcome accepted_baseline_red carrying: the failing test ids, the base sha, the rerun-alone result of each id, and the run ids. It is verifiable later (ddflow verify evidence <id> re-checks that each id still fails on that sha and that the rerun-alone result stands) and it EXPIRES when main is green or the base sha is no longer an ancestor of main: an expired acceptance shows as unproven in status and doctor. Free-form 'forced' stays for cases with no evidence and is counted and shown separately, so it carries information again.
data.title: Forced completion over a red suite becomes a checkable 'accepted baseline-red with evidence' state

data.alternatives: Wildcard approvals for a command family (rejected: too broad); a longer standing window (rejected: governance, see D-standing-window).
data.consequences: Digest and spend logic gain a per-recipe structure; person-only rules (what a person must see) are unchanged: the person sees the whole list and each command.
data.context: Each approval is bound to the exact state and directory it was filed from; one pins regenerate invalidated the next, so four recipes took four serial operator round trips and stale requests piled up.
data.decision: An approval request may name an ordered list of recipes (for example four pins regenerate recipes). The digest binds each recipe to its command, its own files and the directory it must run from; the approval is spent recipe by recipe, in order, and a recipe whose own files are unchanged stays approved when an earlier recipe regenerates other files. The request is filed from the project root or refuses with the directory to use. A change to a file a recipe owns, or a changed command, voids only that recipe.
data.title: An approval can cover an ordered recipe LIST, bound to the files each recipe owns, not to the whole tree state

data.alternatives: Every lane regenerates everything (status quo, rejected); freeze pins (rejected: goldens must follow intended changes).
data.consequences: Needs a write-attribution seam and a lane that owns refresh; interacts with the pins merge driver (B8bb24fad16).
data.context: Four pins were stale from main's drift (golden-snapshots, result-schemas, setup-ops-transcript, loop-transcript) so every lane recorded them as baseline noise; regenerate recorded other lanes' drift and each diff was audited by hand; unknown writers dirtied README.md, default.toml and cli.py in the primary and blocked merges.
data.decision: (1) A 'pins refresh main' job runs once per main commit (queue tail or schedule tick), owned by one lane at a time, and commits only generated files through a merge like any item. (2) 'ddflow pins regenerate' in an item records and writes only the hunks its own diff causes (attributed by the item's changed files); drift from other lanes is reported, not recorded. (3) No gate, hook or ci run writes into the primary checkout; any write there is attributed (writer command, agent, time) in doctor so an unknown writer is named.
data.title: Generated pins on main have one owner: a pins refresh job per main commit; items regenerate only their own hunks; the primary checkout is never written by a gate or hook

data.alternatives: Remove inheritance outright (rejected: some phases rely on it); edit needs by hand (status quo).
data.consequences: Existing phases keep inherit-to-tasks until migrated; a migration note and a doctor note list phases whose tasks inherit.
data.context: Docs-wave edges blocked claims on five phases and a completion on one; they were lifted by hand, each with a hand-written decision (B439e15835c).
data.decision: A phase gains needs_apply = phase (the phase itself cannot start or close until its needs are done; its tasks do not inherit) | tasks (tasks inherit; the historical behaviour) with default phase for new phases once B439e15835c is fixed. 'ddflow phase lift <id> --need <id> --reason ...' removes one edge with a recorded decision, an event and a doctor entry listing active lifts; it is person-or-policy gated like other holds.
data.title: Phase needs: an explicit per-phase flag says whether the phase's own tasks inherit them; a one-command audited lift

data.alternatives: Keep shell-loop heartbeats (rejected: they outlive items); shorter TTLs (rejected: lease lost during long reviews, see fix-B-lease-ttl-expires-during-review).
data.consequences: Builds on DX-lease-release-early (release at merge-ready, decided 2026-11-02) and LK-observed-globs; narrowing must never drop a file with uncommitted changes.
data.context: Whole-directory leases and hot files stalled the P-swarm launcher chain; heartbeat shell loops outlived completed items and a pkill hook blocked stopping them; narrowing a lease needed a manual 'ddflow update --globs'.
data.decision: (1) 'ddflow gate run' and 'ddflow merge' renew the lease for as long as they run and stop when they end; agents never run a heartbeat shell loop, and a heartbeat for an item that is completed, released or abandoned is a harmless no-op that says so. (2) At the first gate and at merge-ready the item's lease narrows to the files it actually wrote (LK-observed-globs data), on a knob, with the dropped globs shown. (3) A lease ends when the item completes; leftover heartbeaters are detected (doctor) with the pid to stop. Directory globs over hot files (core/model.py, cli.py, README.md, default.toml) are warned about at claim with the file-level alternative.
data.title: Leases follow the work automatically: gate run and merge heartbeat themselves, leases narrow to the files written, and a lease ends when the item completes

data.budget: one day; read-only plus a scratch run
data.claim: A conservative reverse-import closure plus a map of data-driven tests (goldens, pins, registries) selects under 15 percent of the suite for a median item with 100 percent recall of historical failures, or falls back to the full suite.
data.falsifier: On the last 100 merges of this repo, a failure of the full suite missing from the selection with no fallback firing, or median selection above 40 percent.
data.mechanism: ast import graph (already used by test_layering) plus a per-test file-touch map recorded from the full run per main sha; data-driven tests keyed to the files they read; unknown file types force the fallback. Prior work: B-gap-affected-tests (abandoned, never built).
data.probe: Replay the last 100 merges: compute the selection from the diff, run the full suite once per merge at -n 48, compare failing ids to the selection.
data.question: Which test-impact selection is safe enough to run per item (full suite only at phase close or on the queue) for a 20k-test suite of about 40 minutes?

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 200-350 lines). Governing decision D-merge-smoke-gate-2026-11-11 (proposed; implement after it is accepted). WHAT: 'ddflow smoke [ITEM]' runs, within [smoke].budget_s (default 60), (1) an import probe of every module the registries list as registering tools, families, commands, config sections or event kinds (derived from the registries, not hand-kept), (2) ruff check and ruff format --check on the changed files, (3) bandit on the changed files with the project's config, (4) the item's own new or changed test files. Outcome passed|failed|unavailable (a missing tool is unavailable, never passed). WHY: main went red twice from merges with partial ci (tool-family import failing for ddflow_dispatch; bandit B608) and every lane then burned a 21600 s ci run that was dead on arrival. ACCEPTANCE: a fixture where a family module fails to import fails smoke in under budget; a fixture with a B608 pattern fails smoke; a missing bandit is unavailable; the probe list equals the registry list (test); runtime on this repo is under budget_s. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Smoke gate: a seconds-long pre-gate (import probe of every tool/family/command/event module, ruff, bandit, targeted tests)

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 100-200 lines). ddflow merge and 'gate run ci' run smoke first on the merge tree; a failed smoke refuses with the failing probe named and starts no suite; an unavailable smoke follows [smoke].on_unavailable (default refuse). The merge queue (BG-ci) runs smoke per member before the batch suite. ACCEPTANCE: merge of a branch with a broken import is refused in seconds and no ci run record exists (test); ci start log shows smoke ran first; knob off restores today's behaviour. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Enforce the smoke gate at merge and ahead of ci: a failing smoke refuses the merge and never starts the full suite

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 100-200 lines). Extends DX-main-red-state (which files the bug and marks main red): while main is red the fix task gets the top priority band in ddflow next and the swarm scheduler, every other merge is refused with the red bug id unless the item names that bug, and the refusal says how long main has been red and the culprit merge. ACCEPTANCE: with main red, next offers the fix task first (test); merge of an unrelated item is refused naming the bug; merge of the fixing item is allowed; green main clears the state. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: A red main prioritises its own fix: the auto-filed bug's fix task is offered first, and only the fixing item may merge

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 200-350 lines). A store keyed by main sha holding per-test-id outcome and failure-text digest (path-normalised), written by the queue or the first full run on that sha and read by ci and unit_tests instead of running a 'clean main worktree' baseline. A missing sha is measured once under the suite lock and stored; a stale or partial store entry is never treated as complete. Related and not duplicated: DX-baseline-red-auto-accept (done: cached run of the base), B48c70b6773 (baseline runs on a newer main than the candidate: the store must key by the candidate's merge-base sha), B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause (store the failure digest, not only the id). ACCEPTANCE: two ci runs on one base sha run the baseline once (test); a different base sha measures again; a worktree-only failure (see GM-lane-testcapable-doctor) is not stored as a baseline failure; entries older than [baseline].keep days are pruned. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Baseline results stored per main commit by test id; ci compares against the cached result for the exact base sha

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 100-200 lines). After a red parallel run, rerun only the failing test ids with no parallelism and a quiet host; classify each id as real (fails alone), parallel_only (passes alone) or unavailable; only real failures count as new or baseline failures, parallel_only is recorded as flaky-under-load with the load average. ACCEPTANCE: a fixture test that fails only under -n 4 is classified parallel_only and does not fail the gate as new; a deterministic failure is real; the rerun is bounded by [baseline].rerun_max_ids (over the cap: unavailable, never passed). Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Tell parallel-run-only failures from real ones: rerun the failing ids alone, serially, and classify them

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 250-400 lines). Governing decision D-accepted-baseline-red-2026-11-11 (proposed). Record outcome accepted_baseline_red on the gate with: failing test ids, failure-text digests, base sha, rerun-alone result per id, run ids. gate status, complete and phase close show it as 'accepted baseline-red (N ids on <sha>)', separately from forced; free-form forced stays but is counted and shown apart. Builds on DX-baseline-red-auto-accept (done) which already measures against a cached base. ACCEPTANCE: a partial unit_tests whose failures all fail on the base sha and fail alone completes as accepted_baseline_red with evidence (test); one new failing id refuses; a forced completion shows under 'forced' not under 'accepted'; phase close lists both counts. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Accepted baseline-red as a distinct, checkable outcome with attached evidence, instead of free-form forced

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 150-250 lines). 'ddflow verify evidence ITEM|PHASE' re-checks that each recorded id still fails on the recorded base sha (store lookup first, a scratch run if absent) and that the base sha is an ancestor of main; an acceptance whose ids now pass on main, or whose sha is gone, shows as expired/unproven in status and doctor. ACCEPTANCE: an acceptance whose ids pass on current main reports expired (test); a rewritten base sha reports unproven; doctor lists unproven acceptances; person-only completion gates are unchanged. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Verify and expire accepted-baseline-red evidence: ddflow verify evidence, and an acceptance expires when main is green

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 100-200 lines). Not the guard bugs themselves (Bc28808f9c3, Bbaaaba1364, Bdc7cd5b259, B19157c3453 are being fixed by agent fix-guard); this is the CHECK that tells us when a lane cannot run tests: 'ddflow doctor --lane ITEM' (and claim, once, on a knob) runs a canary: one real test file plus 'ddflow pins regenerate --check' from the worktree and compares with the same run in the primary, naming the difference (path leakage, a missing editable install, an env var such as CLAUDECODE). ACCEPTANCE: a fixture worktree that cannot import the package is reported not test-capable with the cause (test); a healthy one passes in under 30 s; the result is cached per worktree and sha. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Doctor and self-check that a lane worktree is test-capable: ci, tests and pins run correctly from a linked worktree

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 60-150 lines). When a pin's generator exits non-zero, prints a traceback, or produces output matching the known error shapes (Traceback, 'No module named', usage errors), 'ddflow pins regenerate' refuses to write it and says which generator failed; a pin file changed only to an error text is also refused by the pins precheck. WHY: from linked worktrees pins were recorded from an error output, so they looked stale on every lane. ACCEPTANCE: a generator that raises leaves the pin file byte-identical and exits non-zero (test); a legitimately empty pin is allowed. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Pins refuse to record an error output as a pin

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 80-150 lines). Failure text that includes the ci tree (temporary merge-tree or worktree path) is rewritten to repo-relative placeholders before digesting and comparing, so the same failure on the base and the candidate has the same digest. Related: B-baseline-red-hides-new-cause (digest compare). ACCEPTANCE: the same failure text from two different tree paths yields one digest (test); a real new message still differs. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Normalise ci-tree paths in failure text so baseline compare does not see old failures as new

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 200-350 lines). Governing decision D-pin-refresh-owner-2026-11-11 (proposed). 'ddflow pins refresh-main' regenerates stale pins at current main in one item-like lane (leased once, queued behind merges), commits them through the normal merge, and records which pins it fixed; runs once per main commit that left a pin stale (tick or queue tail), never concurrently. Other lanes see 'pins stale on main, refresh owned by <lane>' and do not record that drift. ACCEPTANCE: with four stale pins on main, one refresh item fixes all four and a second concurrent call refuses naming the owner (test); lanes' pins precheck distinguishes main-stale from item-stale. Related: GM-pins (done), DX-pins-merge-gate, B8bb24fad16. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: A 'pins refresh main' job: one lane owns pin refresh per main commit

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 150-300 lines). Regenerating in an item diffs the regenerated pin against the item's base and keeps only hunks attributable to the item's changed files (by the generator's input map); hunks caused by main drift are reported as 'drift, owned by pins refresh main' and left out of the item's diff. Also covers the pins merge driver keeping an older generated README region: the driver must prefer the side that regenerates from the merged tree (see B8bb24fad16, which fixes the driver itself). ACCEPTANCE: a fixture with one item hunk and one drift hunk commits only the first (test); the report names the second; a pin whose generator cannot attribute falls back to the whole file with a notice. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: pins regenerate records only the hunks the item caused

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 200-350 lines). Gates, hooks and ci never write into the primary checkout (a test runs every gate against a fixture primary and asserts it stays clean). For writes by anything else, doctor and the merge refusal on a dirty primary name who wrote what: the writer is taken from a write-time marker (command, agent, pid, time) written by ddflow's own writers, and an unmarked change is reported as 'unknown writer' with mtime and the last ddflow commands near it. WHY: README.md, default.toml and cli.py generated or format edits appeared in the primary and blocked merges with no owner. Related: B6b7e47955e (merge refuses on the primary's uncommitted agent shard). ACCEPTANCE: a dirty README.md with no marker is reported unknown writer with mtime; with a marker it names the command; the merge refusal prints both. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: The primary checkout is never written by a gate or hook; any other write is attributed to a writer

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 100-250 lines plus a report). Record the result in research R-test-impact-selection-2026-11-11 (verdict CONFIRMED or REFUTED). Replay the last 100 merges: selection from the diff by reverse-import closure plus a file-touch map, full suite at -n 48 once per merge, compare failing ids. Prior: B-gap-affected-tests (abandoned). ACCEPTANCE: report gives recall, median selected share, fallback rate; decision to build TS-impact-select is made from it. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Probe test-impact selection on the last 100 merges (recall and selected share)

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 300-450 lines). Builds the selector the probe validates (revives the scope of abandoned B-gap-affected-tests): per-item unit_tests runs the selection, recorded as outcome partial with the selection reason, never passed; any file the graph cannot map, or a selection over [tests].select_max_share, falls back to the full suite. The full suite runs at phase close (DX-phase-acceptance-full-suite) and by the merge queue once per main commit. ACCEPTANCE: fixture package: a leaf change selects exactly its tests (test); an unmappable file falls back; recall on the probe replay is 100 percent or the fallback fires. Related: FT-pipeline (narrowed tests in the fast pipeline uses this selector). Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Select the tests a change touches for an item; the full suite runs at phase close or on the queue

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 200-350 lines). The suite lock admits N concurrent suites (N from [suites].max_concurrent, default derived from cores) and holds a new suite while the host load average exceeds [suites].load_ceiling_per_core; the wait reason and load are shown in gate status and the queue position is listed; per-test timeouts are not shortened by waiting (see DX-ci-timeout-excludes-queue). WHY: six suites at once starved each other (load 53-85 against a 420 s per-test timeout). ACCEPTANCE: with the ceiling exceeded a second suite waits and says why (test with a fake load source); a timeout fixture shows the per-test clock starting at admission; cap and ceiling are knobs. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Record a decision or lesson only if a surprise appears. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: A load budget and concurrency cap for suites: admit a suite only when the host has headroom

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 250-400 lines). Governing decision D-approval-recipe-list-2026-11-11 (proposed; implement after accepted). An approval request may carry an ordered list of recipes; the digest binds each to its command, the files it owns and its directory; spend is per recipe in order; regenerating one recipe's files does not void another recipe's approval, a change to a recipe's own files or command voids only that recipe. The person sees the whole list. ACCEPTANCE: 4 pins recipes need one approval and one answer (test); an earlier recipe's output leaves a later recipe's approval valid; editing a later recipe's file voids only it; person-only rules unchanged. Related: B61dfe8d120 (chained approvals bug) is the defect; this is the design that removes the chain. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Approve an ordered recipe LIST in one approval, bound to each recipe's own files

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 80-150 lines). 'approvals request' from a linked worktree, a subdirectory or another checkout either normalises to the project root recorded in the request (and shows it) or refuses naming the directory to use; a request whose bound directory differs from where it is spent says so, not 'stale'. ACCEPTANCE: request from a subdirectory yields the root-bound digest equal to the one from the root (test); from a lane worktree the refusal names the primary root. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Filing an approval from the wrong directory is hard: refuse with the right directory, or bind to the project root

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 120-220 lines). Prints for any request its approver class (operator answer with channel and level, standing-window rule with its id and expiry, policy rule, retry rule, none), the evidence record (transcript attest id, rule match text, window start), and shows the class as a column in 'approvals list' and 'log'; policy and window approvals are marked 'automatic' so a report does not call them operator-approved. WHY: approvals showed approved that the operator never answered. ACCEPTANCE: an approval under a standing window reports window rule + expiry (test); an operator answer reports channel and attest id; an unexplained approval is flagged anomaly. Related: GR-approval-evidence. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: ddflow approvals why ID: who or what approved it, with the evidence

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 100-200 lines). 'approvals pending' (exists) groups requests by chain, marks those whose bound state or directory no longer matches as stale and those superseded by a newer request for the same recipe, and 'approvals withdraw --stale' withdraws them (agent may withdraw its own; never approves). ACCEPTANCE: after a pins regenerate the earlier requests show stale with the reason (test); withdraw --stale removes only stale ones; the person-answered list is untouched. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: approvals pending marks stale and superseded requests and withdraws them in one command

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 150-300 lines). Governing decision D-lease-lifecycle-automation-2026-11-11 (proposed). 'ddflow gate run' and 'ddflow merge' renew the item's lease on an interval while they run and stop when they exit or the process dies; agents need no heartbeat loop. 'ddflow heartbeat' for a completed, released or abandoned item returns success with 'item is completed; nothing to renew' and does not extend anything. 'doctor' lists heartbeat-looking processes whose item is finished (pid, command line) so the operator can stop them, and the pkill hook message says how. ACCEPTANCE: a 10-minute fake gate keeps its lease with no external heartbeat (test with a short TTL); after the run no renewal occurs; a heartbeat on a completed item does not touch the lease. Related: fix-B-lease-ttl-expires-during-review, fix-B-long-ci-run-holds-globs-while-waiter-asks-yield. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: gate run and merge heartbeat the lease themselves; no shell loops; a heartbeat for a finished item is a no-op

data.body: Estimated size: S (about 80-160 lines). Completing an item releases every lease still held for it (merge already releases at merge-ready by LK-release-at-merge; this covers the items that complete without a merge, abandon, forced and PR flow), and doctor flags a lease whose item is completed with the lease id. ACCEPTANCE: a completed item holds no lease (test); a completed item with a leaked lease from an old log is flagged by doctor and 'doctor --fix' releases it. Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: A lease ends when the item completes; leftover leases and their holders are reported

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 200-350 lines). At the first gate and at merge-ready the item's lease narrows from its declared globs to the files it changed (committed or in the worktree), using the data LK-observed-globs records, behind [locks].auto_narrow (default on for dir-wide globs over hot files, off otherwise until measured). Dropped globs are listed in the result and in 'ddflow show'; a file with uncommitted changes is never dropped; widening later re-acquires per file. Replaces the manual 'ddflow update --globs'. ACCEPTANCE: an item declaring ddflow/** that wrote 3 files holds 3 files after the first gate (test); another item can then claim a disjoint file under ddflow/; the uncommitted-file case keeps it. Related: DX-lease-release-early (release at merge-ready), DX-lease-real-overlap (done). Tests first: each test below must fail against the unfixed code. Docs: README row, help topic, knob register entry.
data.title: Automatic lease narrowing to the files an item actually wrote, with the dropped globs shown

data.body: Estimated size: M (about 150-300 lines). Governing decision D-phase-needs-scope-2026-11-11 (proposed). Defect side is B439e15835c (a phase's own tasks inherit its needs, so docs-wave edges blocked claims on five phases and a completion on one); this task is the explicit semantics: 'phase add/update --needs-apply phase|tasks', shown in 'phase show', effective-edge views and 'why blocked' naming the inheritance path. Default for new phases is phase; existing phases are listed by doctor as inheriting, with a one-line migration. ACCEPTANCE: a task under a needs_apply=phase phase is claimable while the phase's need is open (test); under tasks it is blocked with the phase edge named; the flag survives replay. data.body:
Main went red at least five times in two days (parity help text, adoption test, transcripts, test_upgrade_apply twice, digest sources) and was found by an unlucky agent's ci. Selective ci misses data-driven tests. Add: (1) every merge triggers a main check (cadence for the full suite), (2) a red result files one bug linked to the first red commit (ddflow bisect) and sets a visible main_red state in status/brief/digest, (3) policy knob: block merges, warn, or auto-revert the culprit merge when a fix does not land in N minutes, (4) stale 'bug filed against a commit already fixed on main' check before an agent spends a run (B3944aebdf3 was already fixed).

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 1): main must also be GREEN-ENFORCED, not only reported: while main is red, merges are refused except the item that fixes it (GM-red-main-priority), and a seconds-long smoke gate (GM-smoke-gate, GM-smoke-enforce, decision D-merge-smoke-gate-2026-11-11) keeps import and bandit failures from reaching main, since two such reds in one day made every lane run a dead-on-arrival 21600 s ci. Acceptance addition: a merge whose smoke fails never produces a red main; a red main refuses unrelated merges naming the bug.

Option B. Entry gets a group id; the integrator merges member tips onto an integration tree, regenerates pins once, runs the full CI set once under the host lock (FIFO), unit_tests full once, roborev range once, then fans out. Folds B-batch-integration (D-BG-10; ddflow task fold when started). Test: 3 members, one ci run, 3 outcomes with covered_by batch. Research docs/ddflow/research/batch-gates.md; proposals docs/ddflow/decisions/batch-gates.md. Start only after BG-decide has recorded the D-BG-* answers (BG-decide is not in needs on purpose, lesson L-needs-on-decide-tasks).

DECIDED 2026-10-22: BG-decide recorded D-BG-Q1..Q10 (all recommended defaults); BG-decide is done, start per needs.

Per D-BG-Q6: run 'ddflow task fold B-batch-integration' into BG-ci when starting. Mode default stays off; ddflow itself turns ci on afterwards (D-BG-Q1).

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 1 and 2): the queue runs the SMOKE gate per member first (GM-smoke-gate), runs the full suite ONCE per main commit, and writes the per-test-id result to the baseline store keyed by sha (GM-baseline-store) so lanes compare against it instead of running a clean-main baseline; failures are rerun alone (GM-rerun-alone) before they count. Decision: D-merge-smoke-gate-2026-11-11.

B-quota-meters: `ddflow gate run <id> ci` with DDFLOW_CI_SUITE_WAIT_S=14400 ended 'ci: UNAVAILABLE, timed out after 3600s' while about seven other lanes held or queued for the suite lock: the [ci].timeout_s clock ran through the wait, so the long wait setting had no effect, and unit_tests then refused to start. Wanted: the run's timeout starts when the suite lock is taken, or the message says the run never started and how far it got in the queue. Acceptance: a test where a run queued past timeout_s still gets its full timeout once it holds the lock.

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 4): six suites at once starved each other (load 53-85 against a 420 s per-test timeout) and the queue wait was recorded as part of the timeout. Acceptance addition: queue wait is recorded separately as queue_wait_s and never counts against timeout_s or a per-test timeout; the admission side (cap and load ceiling) is SL-suite-load-budget.

Select the lightened pipeline from the guard result using the pipeline_by_diff pattern: one combined single-round review (reviewer independence rules unchanged), tests narrowed to affected ones, shared full ci, regression test failing first, dedupe and bug_hunt kept. Config section [fasttrack] (mode off|bundle|lighten, max_bundle 10, max_src_lines 10, max_files 6, max_src_files 2, hot_globs, bundle_max_age_min 45, auto_merge). CONFORMANCE (r-bounded-everything, r-evidence-over-assertion, r-unavailable-not-pass, r-upgrade-safe, r-everything-configurable, r-small-files, r-reuse-core, r-no-shell, r-tell-dont-discover, D-fast-track-answers, D-BG-Q4, D-reviewer-independence-soft, D-baseline-red-auto-accept): the diff decides the pipeline (pattern: services/docsonly.py pipeline_by_diff); demote never promotes; the regression test must fail before the fix; a reviewer or tool that could not run is unavailable, never passed; every number is a [fasttrack] knob settable four ways, company floors tighten-only; ships off for existing projects; extend P-batch-gates BG-*, TA-fastlane, OPT-* instead of a second implementation. Research: R-tiny-fix-fast-track.

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 3): 'tests narrowed to affected ones' is supplied by TS-impact-select (probe first: TS-impact-probe, research R-test-impact-selection-2026-11-11). Small items run the selection (outcome partial), the full suite runs at phase close or on the queue. Add TS-impact-select to needs when this task is started.

One chat answer clears an approval without typing an id. Trust model unchanged: the transcript is editable, so attest records only that a person answered. SIZE M, RISK medium. FALSIFIER: one chat answer clears an approval. Relates to NS-attest-remote. CONFORMANCE (r-everything-configurable, r-tell-dont-discover, r-no-shell, r-safe-by-default, r-docs-with-the-change, D-scope-focus-2026-11, R-audit-ux): every new limit, budget or default is a knob with a check; refusals name the next call in CLI and MCP form; nothing new is CLI-only unless person-only; new enforcement ships warn or off; docs change with the code.

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 6): 'approvals ask' must print the AskUserQuestion payload READY TO USE (the exact tool input, with question, header, options and the answer-to-attest mapping), as JSON on --json and as a copy-ready block otherwise, so a coordinator never hand-parses it. Acceptance addition: the printed payload validates against the AskUserQuestion input shape (test) and one attest call per answered question records the approval. Related: RA-recipe-list (one question for a recipe list), RA-stale-sweep.

fx-Ba2df74d558 held ddflow/infra/log.py, tests/golden/** and ddflow/core/redact* for hours, blocking three other agents, while it only waited on CI. Release files no longer changed (hand back on 'ddflow update --globs'), auto-release after a merge of those files, and show 'held for N hours, last write M minutes ago' in the refusal.

DECIDED 2026-11-02 (D-lock-lifecycle-answers): release at MERGE-READY, never at review start: measured 84 percent of tasks commit again after their first review starts (median 91 min later). Re-acquire per file and sync first when a review asks for edits; the conflict probe (LK-conflict-probe) at release and at merge and ci on the merge result stay mandatory.

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 9): the lease is also DOWNGRADED during gates and reviews (held read-only on files not touched since the last commit, re-acquired per file on the next edit); heartbeats come from gate run and merge themselves (LK-auto-heartbeat), narrowing to written files is automatic (LK-auto-narrow), completion ends the lease (LK-lease-ends-on-complete); decision D-lease-lifecycle-automation-2026-11-11.

Observed: globs declared at claim (ddflow/services/gates/**, tests/golden/**) overlap by PREFIX (L-glob-prefix-overlap), hold files nobody touches, and block parallel agents for hours; agents then pile up uncommitted work. Design: claim records intent globs as advisory; the pre-commit/pre-edit hook acquires a lease on the EXACT files being changed when they are free (and queues/waits with the holder named when not); files are released when merged or idle. Keep [lease].shared_globs (generated/pinned outputs) and new_file_globs exempt. A knob chooses declared (today) vs lazy.

DECIDED 2026-11-02 (D-lock-lifecycle-answers): lock-at-first-write is ENFORCED from the start (no log-only period), knob [locks].mode, org-lockable. Hook transport and cost are LK-hook-snapshot and LK-write-hook-wire.

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 9): whole-directory leases and hot files (core/model.py, cli.py, README.md, default.toml) stalled the P-swarm launcher chain. Add: a claim whose glob is a directory over any hot file warns and proposes the file-level alternative (the hot-file list is derived from lease-wait measurements, LK-measure); acceptance addition: a claim of ddflow/** is refused or warned with the list of hot files it would hold.

Fixes bug B506aa72f8e: Every event-log append (claim/merge/complete) emits one stderr warning per [[reviewer]]: 'sets family, gates, hedge, max_chunk_chars, ... which this ddflow does not know; skipped. The config is newer than this code: merge main into this tree'. It is FALSE: ddflow.services.review.model.Reviewer knows every one of those fields. The warning comes from ddflow/infra/log/_eventlog.py::_reviewer_redact_names, which reads reviewers.toml against the deliberately-narrow _LocalReviewer (name/model/base_url only, to keep the log layer from importing services.review) with lenient=True, so tomlcfg._check treats family/gates/etc as unknown and prints the misleading 'newer than this code' remedy. The narrowing is intentional, not a newer config. The false alarm misled sibling lanes f3-kilo and bug3-kilo into declaring a repo-wide 'all reviewers skipped, rubber_duck/critic cannot run, every complete is a person-gate' blocker when ddflow reviewers list + load_reviewers show grok-4.7 (xai) and gemini-3.5-flash-lite (google) still serving critic+rubber_duck. Fix: _reviewer_redact_names should read the file without the 'does not know/newer than code' warning (its _LocalReviewer view is intentional), or pass a quiet-skip signal to _check.

Write the regression test first and watch it FAIL on the unfixed code; then `ddflow complete fix-B506aa72f8e --regression-test <test>` closes the bug with the task (or `ddflow bug fixed B506aa72f8e --regression-test <test>` first).

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 14): the 'reviewers.toml config is newer than this code' warning prints on every command, including when the installed ddflow differs from the repo code. Acceptance addition: print it at most once per process and once per ddflow version per hour (stamp in .ddflow/local), say which ddflow (installed or repo) is older, and never on read-only list/show commands; a test counts occurrences over three commands.

A field on tasks the operator may set (and an agent may propose, which the operator confirms); used as a prior in ETA-model and shown next to the prediction; never overrides the observed data once enough samples exist. Tests first.

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 14): 'ddflow task add --line/--lines' mean RELEASE lines, which agents read as a size. This task supplies the size field ('--size XS|S|M|L' or an estimate) so the UX-release-line-flag help can point at it; check GV-complexity-score for the derived score so the two are not both hand-set.

Operator asked 2026-10-26 to prevent ruff-format failures. Options: a pre-commit hook that formats staged Python files with ruff format (fix mode, restage), ddflow merge running ruff format on the merged diff's Python files as a bot commit, a gate check in standards, and a line in the agent brief (L-format-python-before-commit). Decide the least surprising combination; keep derived formatting out of review diffs (D-lean-review risk tiers).

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (environment observation c): the autoformat hook in agents' worktrees staged a reformat of files OUTSIDE the item's lease. Acceptance addition: the formatter touches only the item's own changed files (never files it did not edit), never re-stages files outside the lease, and lists what it reformatted; see the bug filed for the staging behaviour.

Reviewer finding on DX-phase-acceptance-full-suite: the phase-close check is time-ordered; a ci run --full on another branch after the last merge satisfies it. Record the tested head sha in cadence.ran evidence and require the phase's merged shas to be ancestors.

AMENDED 2026-11-11: phase close automation (sha ancestry, evidence record) is CO-phase-close; the sha equivalence check is VF-verify-shas. Keep this task to recording the tested sha on the integration_tests pass.

SIZE M, RISK med. Found by R-scheduler-2026-11-11: triggers.evaluate is reachable only from api.schedule.trigger_evaluate and nothing calls it automatically. This task is the single entry point: tick(now) evaluates due schedules (B-sched-due) and event triggers (B-trigger-model), files items, writes trigger.evaluated, under a lock with a time budget and the global hourly cap; callers: brief, session start, after worktree.merged and item completion, loop ticks, and the CLI/MCP verb 'schedule tick' for external schedulers (B-sched-emitters prints the line that runs it; ADP-scheduler registers it). No daemon. Concurrent ticks collapse to one (lease on the tick). Acceptance: two ticks at once file once; a tick after 10 days of outage files once per job (missed policy), no storm; a tick on a clean repo costs no git call beyond the facts requested. Part of R-scheduler-2026-11-11. Hard limits: no daemon (D-sched-no-daemon-r2); a job only files items or runs a read-only check (D-trigger-actions-create-items); verbs ride B-sched-author's family, do not edit cli.py, mcp.py or config.py; literal globs only. Every cap is bounded with a visible stop (r-bounded-everything). Tests fail before the change, fake clock.

AMENDED by D-scheduler-answers-2026-11-11 (answer 2): when a due job is mutating, the tick files the approval request and parks the run instead of running it, records schedule.run outcome awaiting_approval, and the next tick does not refile while the request is pending or after it was answered (idempotent per job+sha+approval); the tick never waits on a person and never auto-approves; parked runs are listed in brief with owner and next call. Acceptance additions: tick with a mutating due job files exactly one request across repeated ticks; approved request later runs once; a rejected or expired request is recorded and obeys the cap and the breaker; tick time budget is unaffected by parked runs.

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 13): the tick is also the fallback delivery path for wake-ups (CO-wake-events): events with a subscriber and no live sink are delivered at the next tick. No change to this task's scope until CO-wake-sinks exists.

Lift the existing [ci].pins_precheck (read-only, bounded ddflow pins regenerate --check) into a first-class CHEAP gate keyed to [pins].merge_check, that a task can run stand-alone before/with the merge gate without paying for the full ci suite. Lock merge on it: if the merged tree carries a stale pin (once fix-merge-result-carries-pins lands the pins field on worktree.merged/MERGE_PAYLOAD), the merge gate refuses and names the fix, and the after-merge hook (fix-B38ceb8819e) re-records the pins in the merge commit. Depends on fix-B38ceb8819e (enforce after_merge regenerate) and fix-merge-result-carries-pins (merge carries pins field).

AMENDED 2026-11-11 (coordinator observation 8): the precheck must tell 'stale on main' (owned by PIN-refresh-main, not this item's) from 'stale because of this item' (PIN-own-hunks); only the latter locks merge.

data.summary: Some tasks complete with no recorded sha ('completed as -'), and some recorded shas are not ancestors of main after history rewrites although an equivalent commit exists.
